1.note: הֲדוֹם is "footstool"; here it is read as the land's low places, set against "its heights" in the line before. "Shone forth" (זָרַחְתִּי) plays on the narrator's name, the Ezrahite.

2.note: Song 4:13 pairs כְּפָרִים (henna) with nard. The same word, pointed כְּפָרִים, means "villages" two lines earlier: a pun that English cannot keep.

3.note: מִשְׁבְּצוֹת are gold settings or woven work (Exod 28:11; Ps 45:14). שָׁנֶיהָ is read as from שָׁנִי, scarlet: the red of sunset. "Her years" is also a possible reading.

4.note: In Lev 1:16 the priest removes the crop of a bird offering. Here it means the dirt of the house, but the bird phrase looks ahead to the cock.

5.note: Literally "the bloods of the heart and the cuts". The sense is uncertain; perhaps the choicest parts of the slaughtered beast.

6.note: בַּבְּקָרִים can be "with the oxen" or "in the mornings"; both fit the line.

7.note: Isa 40:6 "all flesh is grass". Here it is taken literally: the dish is greens, not meat. This prepares the narrator's craving for the cock.

8.note: The cock recites the morning blessing (b. Berakhot 60b), built on Job 38:36 "who has given understanding to the שֶׂכְוִי", a word the rabbis read as "cock".

9.note: The law of the bird's nest (Deut 22:7). The cock applies it to himself: let the parent go and take the young.

10.he: וְקִדַּמְתִּים בְּבָנִים גַּם בְּבָנוֹת / וְהֵם בַּמַּאֲכֶלֶת קִדְּמוּנִי
10.note: קִדֵּם is "come before, meet (with a gift)"; the verb repeats in both halves. Read as: I met them with gifts of sons and daughters, they met me with the knife.

11.he: עַל הַנִּסִּים וְעַל הַפֻּרְקָן וְעַל הַפְּדוּת וְעַל הַתְּשׁוּעָה
11.note: The words of the liturgical thanksgiving "Al ha-Nissim" ("for the miracles"), said on Ḥanukkah and Purim.

12.note: A play on עֶצֶם (bone) and the verb עִצֵּם, "break the bones" (Jer 50:17). The rendering of the last verb is uncertain.

13.note: A pun on the name חֶבֶר (Ḥever) and מְחַבֵּר, "joins, composes". The next line goes on with אַחְבִּיר from the same root (Job 16:4).
